summary: The solver-visible continuity controller is a substantive, reachable production-style system rather than LOC padding. The real continuityctl entrypoint binds the active ContinuityEngine into a shared operator CLI that drives SQLite durable state, real local NATS JetStream domains, stream/source topology bootstrap, publication, archive synchronization, durable consumer effects and checkpoints, reconciliation, generation authority, replay, recovery leases/fencing, retention and health reporting. Major modules are behaviorally differentiated and mutually dependent. The 12,000-event seeded incident and operator artifacts populate the same state model consumed by runtime branches, including archive gaps, consumer lag, duplicate-effect exposure, an active replay plan and unsafe cleanup state. Cross-module invariants create genuine partial-fix traps, and removing roughly a quarter of the core would eliminate material operational behavior. No material Q6 production-logic defect was found within the packet-authorized evidence boundary.

evidence.observation: Q6 requires independent assessment of entrypoint reachability, substantive branching/state/persistence/integration behavior, module differentiation, meaningful state volume, cross-module partial-fix traps, removal impact, and padding risk; raw LOC or other gate verdicts are insufficient.

The required method traces real entrypoints and major modules, checks wrappers/clones/unreachable filler, identifies partial-fix traps, applies a roughly 25% removal test, and requires at least 3,000 substantive reachable solver-visible runtime/config LOC for large_system_strict.
The solver-visible operator executable directly invokes python -m continuity.starter_cli under the task runtime root; it is not a verifier-only launcher.

The inherited operator surface binds cli.ContinuityEngine to the active engine.ContinuityEngine and then delegates to the shared cli.main, while database initialization applies the runtime schema extension. Starter behavior therefore traverses the same CLI/runtime/store path a repair changes.

The shared CLI constructs ContinuityStore plus ContinuityEngine from durable state/config and exposes operational commands for health, reconciliation, generation decisions, replay planning/execution, recovery leases, retention, NATS lab lifecycle, archive sync, durable consumers, reset and final verification.

Runtime code performs real NATS connections and JetStream API requests, validates publish acknowledgements, creates/updates streams and durable consumers, pulls and acks/naks messages, synchronizes hub messages into the archive index, and starts/stops three nats-server processes with readiness monitoring.

The controller implements topology/policy interpretation, publication state transitions, generation validation, differentiated consumer effects, effect/checkpoint sequencing, identity-based reconciliation, replay plans, lease/fence checks, replay execution, retention decisions/application and composite health reporting.

The active inherited controller overrides production methods on the real operator path, including publication, generation observation, consumer dispatch/effect processing, reconciliation, replay planning, recovery ownership and retention. The override layer changes operational state behavior rather than adding decorative modules or constant-output shells.

The SQLite store uses WAL and explicit transactions and persists publish attempts, generation transitions, archive identity/collisions, idempotent effects, separate ack/effect checkpoints, reconciliation runs/findings, replay plans/items, recovery leases, retention watermarks/holds and a multi-table state digest.

The domain model enforces stable region/generation/origin event identity, envelope integrity, subjects, stream/source topology, retention horizon arithmetic, replay ranges/status, lease owner/epoch/expiry fencing and reconciliation/health semantics.

The durable schema contains interrelated tables and constraints for regions, origin generations, a local event journal, publish attempts, archive identity, consumer registry/effects/checkpoints, poison events, reconciliation, replay, leases, retention and operator actions rather than disconnected fixture tables.

Runtime extensions add persisted effect dispatch observations and origin observations used by the active controller, reinforcing crash/idempotency and generation-state behavior rather than static volume.

The deterministic seed creates 12,000 varied telemetry events across two regions and 240 devices, with publish states/attempts, archive membership and deliberate gaps, duplicate observations, two required consumer effect histories at different progress points, retention watermarks and an approved replay plan. This volume is directly queried and mutated by production logic.

The configuration defines distinct east/west JetStream domains, a hub archive with source bindings and subject transforms, three consumers with different effect roles/criticality, and recovery/retention timing consumed by the runtime and controller.

The operator handoff describes a carrier disconnect/reconnect, five archive identity gaps, divergent application versus JetStream consumer progress, a duplicate effect, cleanup conflicting with consumer/replay authority, and generation-reset handling; these states correspond to the shipped durable model and operational commands.

The incident log records concrete journal/archive counts, duplicate publish attempts, effect redelivery, checkpoint divergence, an approved replay range, retention inputs and an operator halt, aligning with the deterministic seeded incident rather than unsupported backstory.

PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Publication identity spans event journal state, publish-attempt message IDs, JetStream expected-stream acknowledgements, generation watermarks and later archive membership; fixing only retry behavior can still duplicate or misclassify archive state.

Origin generation changes alter accepted event identity and therefore validation, reconciliation grouping, replay ranges/items and checkpoint namespaces; treating a lower sequence as ordinary lag breaks multiple subsystems.

Durable consumer correctness crosses JetStream delivery/ack behavior, processing_effects idempotency, effect dispatch, and separate acknowledgement versus application-effect checkpoints, exposing crash/redelivery ordering failures that local ack-only fixes do not solve.

Replay execution consumes persisted plans/items, journal events, current archive membership, publication logic and recovery lease/fence state; ownership can become stale during a multi-item replay and must affect mutation paths continuously.

Retention eligibility is coupled to archive progress, the slowest required consumer, active replay pinning, age and per-event hold state plus the stream horizon; an archive-only cleanup rule can delete required replay/application authority.

Hub topology is consumed by RuntimeBootstrap source transforms and ArchiveSynchronizer interpretation, so a source-domain/config correction must agree with model topology validation and downstream origin metadata.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: PASS. Removing roughly one quarter of the core cannot be done without deleting a material production capability: removing runtime.py eliminates live JetStream topology/publication/consumer/archive behavior; removing store.py/SQL eliminates durable continuity state and crash/idempotency semantics; removing policy.py/engine.py eliminates the cross-subsystem state machine and recovery/retention logic; removing model.py eliminates identity/topology/fence invariants; removing the CLI/binding layer disconnects operator workflows from the implementation. The system is therefore not a large decorative shell around a small grading core.
